facts.fact: The vendor (Adwave) states that average CTV ad video completion rates are 92-97%.
facts.quote: **CTV ads:** 92-97% completion rate

facts.fact: The vendor states that average completion rates for YouTube skippable ads are 15-30%.
facts.quote: **YouTube skippable ads:** 15-30% completion rate

facts.fact: The vendor states that YouTube non-skippable ads have a 70-80% completion rate but are limited to 15-20 seconds.
facts.quote: **YouTube non-skippable ads:** 70-80% completion rate (but limited to 15-20 seconds)

facts.fact: The vendor states that the YouTube skip button appears after 5 seconds for skippable ads.
facts.quote: Skip button appears after 5 seconds (for skippable ads)

facts.fact: The vendor states that YouTube TrueView (skippable) ads cost $0.10-$0.30 per view.
facts.quote: **CPV (Cost Per View):** $0.10-$0.30 for TrueView (skippable) ads

facts.fact: The vendor states that YouTube non-skippable and bumper ads cost $10-$30 CPM.
facts.quote: **CPM:** $10-$30 for non-skippable and bumper ads

facts.fact: The vendor states that YouTube advertising has no minimum budget.
facts.quote: **Minimum budget:** No minimum; start with any amount

facts.fact: The vendor defines a YouTube view as 30 seconds watched, or the full video if it is shorter.
facts.quote: **View definition:** 30 seconds watched (or full video if shorter)

facts.fact: The vendor states that CTV CPM ranges from $15-$35, with an average of $25 for small businesses.
facts.quote: **CPM:** $15-$35 (average $25 for small businesses)

facts.fact: The vendor states that Adwave's CTV advertising starts at $30 per day.
facts.quote: **Minimum budget:** Varies; [Adwave](https://adwave.com/) starts at $30 a day

facts.fact: The vendor defines a CTV view as full ad completion, typically for 15-30 second ads.
facts.quote: **View definition:** Full ad completion (typically 15-30 seconds)

facts.fact: In the vendor's illustrative $500 example, YouTube yields roughly 20,000-50,000 impressions and 3,000-15,000 completed views.
facts.quote: **YouTube:** Roughly 20,000-50,000 impressions, but only 3,000-15,000 completed views (depending on format)

facts.fact: In the vendor's illustrative $500 example, CTV yields roughly 14,000-20,000 impressions and 13,000-19,000 completed views.
facts.quote: **CTV:** Roughly 14,000-20,000 impressions, with 13,000-19,000 completed views

facts.fact: The vendor gives an example of a local business with $1,000/month for video advertising splitting $600 to CTV and $400 to YouTube.
facts.quote: A local business with $1,000/month for video advertising might split:

facts.fact: The vendor states that YouTube bumper ads are 6 seconds long.
facts.quote: YouTube's bumper ads (6 seconds) and skippable formats work well

facts.fact: The vendor states that CTV ads are typically produced in a 30-second standard format.
facts.quote: 30-second format is standard

facts.fact: The vendor states that CTV geographic targeting can go down to ZIP code level.
facts.quote: **Geographic precision:** Down to ZIP code level

facts.fact: The vendor states that YouTube's audience of ages 18-34 spends significant time on the platform.
facts.quote: **Your target demographic skews young:** Younger audiences (18-34) spend significant time on YouTube.

facts.fact: The vendor states that YouTube is the world's second-largest search engine.
facts.quote: YouTube is the world's second-largest search engine.

facts.fact: YouTube creative formats the page lists as needed include 6-second bumpers, 15-second non-skippable ads, and 30-second-plus skippable ads.
facts.quote: Multiple formats needed (6s bumpers, 15s non-skip, 30s+ skippable)

facts.fact: The page advises that YouTube ads hook viewers within the first 5 seconds, before the skip button appears.
facts.quote: Hook in first 5 seconds (before skip button appears)

facts.fact: The page states that YouTube's most common format (TrueView) lets viewers skip after 5 seconds.
facts.quote: YouTube's most common format (TrueView) allows viewers to skip after 5 seconds.

facts.fact: The page states that most CTV ads are non-skippable, so viewers watch the full 15- or 30-second commercial.
facts.quote: Most CTV ads are non-skippable, which means viewers watch your full 15 or 30-second commercial.

facts.fact: The page says non-skippable YouTube ads exist but cost more than skippable ones, with no dollar figure given.
facts.quote: Non-skippable YouTube ads exist but cost more.

facts.fact: The page suggests that very small budgets of $50-200 per month might start with one platform, while larger budgets can test both.
facts.quote: Very small budgets ($50-200/month) might start with one platform.

facts.fact: The page names Hulu, Peacock, and Roku as examples of streaming services where CTV ads run.
facts.quote: CTV (Connected TV) advertising refers to ads on streaming services like Hulu, Peacock, Roku, and others, viewed on TV screens.
